summary: A shevuas ha'eidus is when people swear that they do not know any testimony for someone. It applies only to people who are allowed to be witnesses. Rabbi Meir and the Sages discuss when they become chayav.

chunks.he: שְׁבוּעַת הָעֵדוּת נוֹהֶגֶת בַּאֲנָשִׁים וְלֹא בְנָשִׁים,
chunks.en: A shevuas ha'eidus applies to men and not to women,
chunks.st: The oath of testimony is practiced with regard to men but not with regard to women,

words.note: Shevuas ha'eidus: witnesses swear that they know no testimony for someone.

chunks.en: to strangers and not to relatives,
chunks.st: with regard to non-relatives of the litigants but not with regard to relatives,

chunks.en: to people fit to be witnesses, and not to people who are not fit.
chunks.st: with regard to those fit to testify but not with regard to those unfit to testify due to a transgression that they performed.

chunks.en: It applies only to people who are able to testify.
chunks.st: And the oath of testimony is practiced only with regard to those fit to testify.

chunks.en: In front of a beis din or not
chunks.st: The oath of testimony is practiced both in the presence of a court and not

chunks.en: But if others make him swear,
chunks.st: But if the oath is administered by others
chunks.stMore: and those denying that they witnessed the incident in question neither take an oath nor answer amen to the administered oath,

chunks.en: they are not chayav until they deny
chunks.st: they are not liable until they deny any knowledge of the incident in question

chunks.en: it in front of a beis din.
chunks.st: in court.

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.he: בֵּין מִפִּי עַצְמוֹ וּבֵין מִפִּי אֲחֵרִים,
chunks.en: Whether he swears by himself or others make him swear,
chunks.st: Whether one of the witnesses takes the oath on his own or whether the oath is administered by others,

chunks.en: they are not chayav until they deny
chunks.st: the witnesses are not liable until they deny any knowledge of the incident in question before the litigants

chunks.en: it in front of a beis din.
chunks.st: in court.

summary: Witnesses who swear falsely bring a korban oleh v'yored. They are chayav if they knew they were witnesses, even if they made a mistake about the oath.

chunks.en: One is chayav for swearing falsely on purpose,
chunks.st: And one is liable for the act of taking a false oath with intent

chunks.en: and for a mistake about the oath, when he knew about the testimony.
chunks.explain: He knew he saw it, but did not know the oath was so serious.
chunks.st: and for an unwitting act of taking a false oath, i.e., he is unaware of the liability for taking a false oath, provided that he takes the oath with intent in terms of the testimony,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he takes an oath that he has no knowledge of the matter even though he knows that he witnessed the incident.

chunks.en: But they are not chayav for a mistake about the testimony.
chunks.explain: They really thought they knew nothing.
chunks.st: But witnesses are not liable for taking the oath if they were unwitting
chunks.stMore: in terms of the testimony, i.e., they believe that they have no knowledge of the matter.

chunks.he: וּמַה הֵן חַיָּבִין עַל זְדוֹן הַשְּׁבוּעָה,
chunks.en: And what are they chayav for swearing falsely on purpose?
chunks.st: And what are they liable for by taking a false oath with intent? They are liable to bring

chunks.en: A korban oleh v'yored.
chunks.st: a sliding-scale offering.

summary: How a shevuas ha'eidus works: the witnesses swear that they know nothing. If he made them swear many times outside beis din and then they denied in beis din, they are chayav for each oath; inside beis din, only once.

chunks.en: How does a shevuas ha'eidus work?
chunks.st: Liability to bring a sliding-scale offering for taking a false oath of testimony, how so?

chunks.en: If someone said to two people, "Come and testify for me,"
chunks.st: In a case where the plaintiff said to two individuals: Come and testify on my behalf, and they replied:

chunks.en: and they said, "We swear we do not know any testimony for you,"
chunks.st: On our oath we do not know any testimony on your

chunks.st: these two witnesses are liable.

chunks.en: If he made them swear five times

chunks.en: in front of beis din, and they denied,
chunks.st: before the court, and they denied knowledge of the incident,

chunks.st: they are liable for taking only one false oath.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said:

chunks.en: What is the reason?
chunks.st: What is the reason for this ruling?

chunks.en: Because they cannot go back and admit.
chunks.explain: Once they denied in beis din, they cannot take it back.
chunks.st: Since once they denied that they had any knowledge of the incident they can no longer retract that denial and admit that they have knowledge of the matter.
chunks.stMore: Therefore, there was only one oath of testimony, and there is no liability for the remaining oaths.

summary: If both witnesses deny together, both are chayav. If one denies after the other, only the first is chayav. With two groups of witnesses, both groups can be chayav.

chunks.en: If both witnesses denied together,
chunks.st: If both of the witnesses denied knowledge of the incident together,

chunks.en: both are chayav.
chunks.st: both of them are liable.

chunks.en: If one after the other,
chunks.st: If they denied knowledge one after the other,

chunks.en: the first is chayav and the second is patur.
chunks.explain: After the first denies, one witness alone cannot win the case.
chunks.st: the first who denied knowledge is liable, and the second is exempt,
chunks.stMore: as once the first witness denies knowledge of the incident, the second is an individual witness, whose testimony is not decisive.

chunks.en: If one denied and one admitted,
chunks.st: If one of the two witnesses denied knowledge of the incident, and the other one admitted that he had knowledge and proceeded to testify,

chunks.en: the one who denied is chayav.
chunks.st: the one who denies knowledge of the incident is liable.

chunks.en: If there were two groups of witnesses,
chunks.st: If there were two sets of witnesses that took the oath of testimony,

chunks.he: כָּפְרָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ כָּפְרָה הַשְּׁנִיָּה,
chunks.en: and the first group denied, and then the second group denied,
chunks.st: and the first set denied knowledge of the matter and then the second set denied knowledge of the matter,

chunks.en: both groups are chayav,
chunks.st: both of the sets are liable,

chunks.en: because either group could have given the testimony.
chunks.st: because the testimony can exist with either of them,
chunks.stMore: as even after the first set denies knowledge of the incident, the second remains capable of providing decisive testimony.

chunks.st: If one says: The Lord God shall strike you (see Deuteronomy 28:22),

chunks.en: or "so may Hashem strike you,"
chunks.st: and likewise if one says: God shall strike you if you do not come to testify,

chunks.en: this is the curse written in the Torah.
chunks.explain: Such an oath counts, and the witnesses are chayav.
chunks.st: that is a curse that is written in the Torah, and in such a case one is certainly liable if he fails to testify.
chunks.stMore: If one says to the witnesses:

chunks.en: If he said, "May Hashem not strike you,"
chunks.st: God shall not strike you, or:

chunks.en: or "May He bless you," or "May He be good to you,"
chunks.st: God shall bless you, or: God shall benefit you if you come and testify,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says they are chayav,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir deems him liable,
chunks.stMore: as one may infer from that statement that if he fails to testify God will strike him, or will not bless or benefit him.

chunks.en: and the Sages say they are patur.
chunks.st: And the Rabbis deem him exempt because the curse is not explicitly stated.
